Hackers targeted water systems in at least seven states. The FBI and EPA issued warnings, noting that these attacks are part of a larger pattern of targeting critical infrastructure.

The Bright Side:
Federal agencies are coordinating more effectively to warn utilities and provide actionable security advice to prevent further service disruptions.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a HOW vs. WHY error. The claim assumes a specific policy decision (HOW) caused the attack (WHY), ignoring the multi-year history of these specific threats.

Social Physics Analysis:
By linking unrelated policy decisions to a specific security failure, the actor uses the event to justify a pre-existing political stance. This projection of motive obscures the technical reality of the threat.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The narrative prioritizes political point-scoring over technical resolution.

The Unavoidable Truth: Critical infrastructure is increasingly vulnerable to remote cyber interference.

The Unavoidable Lie: A single policy shift is the sole cause of these complex international cyber threats.

Reducing systemic security failures to a single political decision is a failure of logic. We must address the technical debt in our infrastructure regardless of the current administration.
